title: The basket in the reeds (Exodus 2:1–10)
hookLine: a mother, a sister watching, and Pharaoh's daughter who pities the child

cards: Pharaoh's order is out: every Hebrew baby boy goes into the Nile. In one house of the tribe of Levi, a boy is born. His mother sees, the text says, that he's a goodly child.
So she hides him. One month. Two.

Three. Three months of a newborn: the crying at three in the morning, the neighbors, the thin walls. When she can't hide him any longer, she does something that sounds like obeying the order and is the opposite.
She puts her son in the Nile. Just not the way Pharaoh meant.

teach.h: A TEVAH: THE SAME WORD AS NOAH'S ARK.
teach.b: First, the basket. She takes a basket of papyrus reeds, seals it with tar and pitch, lays the baby inside, and sets it among the reeds at the river's edge.
The Hebrew word for this basket is tevah, the same word Genesis uses for Noah's ark: a boat that carries life through deadly water, this time the size of a baby. Second, the sister.

teach.h: A SISTER STANDS AT A DISTANCE.
teach.b: She stands at a distance, the text says, to see what will happen. She isn't named here; later the Bible names Moses's sister as Miriam, and tradition takes her to be this girl. Third, Pharaoh's daughter.
She comes down to bathe, sees the basket, sends her maid to fetch it, and opens it. The baby is crying.

teach.h: ONE OF THE BABES OF THE HEBREWS.
teach.b: She has compassion on him, and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "This is one of the babes of the Hebrews." She knows exactly what he is, and whose order he's under: her father's. And she pities him anyway.
Fourth, the sister's move. Quick as anything, she steps out: shall I go and find you a nurse from the Hebrew women? Go, says the princess, and the girl fetches the baby's own mother.
Pharaoh's daughter even pays her to nurse her own son.

When he's older, the princess adopts him and names him Moses, because, she says, she drew him out of the water. So count the women before Moses says a single word: two midwives, a mother, a sister, a princess.
The king's plan was to drown the boys. Every one of those women undid it.

how: Matthew's Gospel tells of the infant Jesus carried to safety in Egypt when Herod ordered the boys of Bethlehem killed, and Catholic preaching sometimes sets that rescue beside the infant Moses saved from a king's order.

games.why: she steps out and asks: shall I go and call a nurse from the Hebrew women? and she brings their own mother.

practice: Think of someone who can't fully protect themselves: a child, a new neighbor still learning the language, an elderly relative, a kid at school who sits alone.
The sister in the reeds didn't rescue anyone; she stayed close enough to see, and spoke up at the right moment, so picture where you could stand and keep watch.
If you pray, hold them before God by name; if you don't, simply keep them in view.
